summary: Planned the answered 'Lock Opportunity Amount after Closed Won' requirement at scale ask into exactly one milestone (M1) and one step (M1-S01, type validation, agent metadata-builder, human_gate false), per standards/build-orchestration.md Section 3.1. The step builds a ValidationRule on Opportunity (bypass -> relevance-gate -> business-rule formula order, PRIORVALUE delta check guarded by NOT(ISNEW())) plus the Sales-Ops-only bypass mechanism (a CustomPermission read via $Permission and a PermissionSet granting it), all four artefacts under artefacts/M1-S01/ so the validation-rules checker's VR-REF-02 $Permission resolution and the custom-permissions checker both run cleanly at step scope. Recorded one fit_gap row (Low-Code, effort M, fit), two decisions (bypass mechanism; deploy active despite historical violations), both resolved via source_reference with adr_required true because no decision tree covers either choice, and six assumptions (A1-A6) for the six informational clarifications (Q8-Q13) that carry a scale:ask pre-filled default rather than a recorded answer. Wrote the plan body via set-plan, validated (0 warnings), ran ensure-gates (3 gates present, nothing to add), and rendered PLAN.md/CLARIFICATIONS.md/RUN.md. Status is now planned; gate 'plan' is pending.
confidence_rationale: Every step field resolves on disk (metadata-builder is class: runtime, status: beta, requires_org: false; both skills, both checkers and the one template all exist; validate exits 0 with 0 steps blocked), which would otherwise clear the HIGH bar, but neither of the two decisions this plan had to make (D1: bypass mechanism; D2: deploy active vs inactive) is settled by a decision-tree branch — both rest on source_reference to admin/validation-rules/SKILL.md and carry adr_required: true, which is the agent's own documented MEDIUM condition.

process_observations.observation: Every blocking clarification (Q1-Q7) arrived with a substantive, org-specific answer rather than a default, so the plan needed no invented fact for volume, bypass ownership, post-save writers, or historical data state — the four things that usually force a step to blocked or an assumption to carry high risk.

A fixture holding exactly M1-S01's four declared outputs ran clean through both cited checkers: check_validation_rules.py exited 0 with one advisory INFO (no field inventory in scope, harmless because Amount and StageName are standard fields), and check_custom_permissions.py exited 0 with zero errors/warnings, confirming VR-REF-02's $Permission resolution works at step scope because the CustomPermission file is co-located with the rule.

M1-S01 grants a CustomPermission and a PermissionSet, which is exactly the access-changing shape the general Step 6 human_gate rule in agents/build-planner/AGENT.md says should be human_gate: true, but the scale:ask override in that same Step 6 forces human_gate: false and folds the decision into the single up-front 'go' gate instead of a per-step approval; the tension is real and this plan follows the more specific, later-stated override.

plan.json still shows Q8-Q13 at status 'open' with no answer field even though scale:ask's contract says informational rows 'land pre-filled from their proposed_default'; CLARIFICATIONS.md renders the same six questions with a blank Answer: line. The pre-fill was applied here at the plan layer as assumptions[] (A1-A6) rather than at the clarifications layer, which is a workable but not obviously the intended place for that state to live.

Whether D1 (custom-permission bypass) and D2 (deploy active despite dirty data) are genuinely 'technology choices the plan makes' or simply an implementation of what Q3 and Q5 already answered verbatim is a judgment call; a plan-verifier or human could reasonably read them as scope items instead of decisions, since the requester's own answer already named the mechanism.

Step 4 rule 2 of agents/build-planner/AGENT.md says 'Set adr_required: true' unconditionally whenever a decision is resolved via source_reference instead of a tree branch, but skills/architect/architecture-decision-records/SKILL.md's own ADR-candidacy bar (multi-quarter impact, reversal of an earlier recorded choice, the 6-month test, and the 'fits in a PR description' exclusion) would not promote either D1 or D2 to a real ADR — both are task-level, feature-internal tradeoffs. Followed the build-planner's literal, mechanical rule rather than the more nuanced ADR bar, since the former is the instruction this run was told to follow exactly.

At feature/project scale this single step would normally split into a validation step (the rule) and a separate access step (the CustomPermission + PermissionSet), each with its own type per standards/build-orchestration.md Section 4's step-type table; scale:ask's exactly-one-step rule forces them into one step typed validation, which is correct per Section 3.1 but means the step's type no longer names everything it produces.
The plan is written, validated (0 warnings) and rendered; the next stage in the loop is the adversarial three-lens verification before the human plan gate.
process_observations.followup_reason: standards/build-orchestration.md Section 3 always routes a planned build to plan-verifier next, before the plan gate can be approved.

process_observations.observation: Both decisions in this plan carry adr_required: true even though neither clears the architecture-decision-records candidacy bar; a Well-Architected pass could confirm that reading or surface a reason this build genuinely does warrant an ADR that this run did not see.
process_observations.followup_reason: Well-Architected review is the agent's own documented follow-up whenever a decision is recorded with adr_required: true.
